## Load data

```{r}
viro <- read.csv("~/GitHub/VirosporeQuant/Optimal.entrap/Data/virospore.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",")

# Subset data for MOI = 0.1
viro.sub <- viro %>%
  filter(MOI == 0.1, !is.na(virospores.ml)) %>%
  mutate(
    time = Infection.time.h,
    y = log10(virospores.ml)
  )

# Check the data used in the analysis
nrow(viro.sub)
summary(viro.sub)

# Observed range of infection time
range(viro.sub$time)
```

## Fit equations with maximum likelihood

### Model 1: Flat baseline + symmetric Gaussian window

```{r}
# Starting values
B0 = min(viro.sub$y)
A = max(viro.sub$y) - min(viro.sub$y)
MU = viro.sub$time[which.max(viro.sub$y)]
SIGMA = 4
Z = sd(viro.sub$y)

fit1 <- mle2(y ~
    dnorm(mean = b0 +
          a * exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)),
          sd = z),
    start = list(b0 = B0, a = A, mu = MU,
                 sigma = SIGMA, z = Z),
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(b0 = -Inf,
              a = 0,
              mu = min(viro.sub$time),
              sigma = 0.001,
              z = 0.001),
    upper = c(b0 = Inf,
              a = Inf,
              mu = max(viro.sub$time),
              sigma = Inf,
              z = Inf),
    data = viro.sub)

summary(fit1)
```

### Model 2: Linear baseline + symmetric Gaussian window

```{r}
# Starting values
B0 = min(viro.sub$y)
B1 = -0.05
A = max(viro.sub$y) - min(viro.sub$y)
MU = viro.sub$time[which.max(viro.sub$y)]
SIGMA = 4
Z = sd(viro.sub$y)

fit2 <- mle2(y ~
    dnorm(mean = b0 + b1 * time +
          a * exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigma^2)),
          sd = z),
    start = list(b0 = B0, b1 = B1, a = A, mu = MU,
                 sigma = SIGMA, z = Z),
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(b0 = -Inf,
              b1 = -Inf,
              a = 0,
              mu = min(viro.sub$time),
              sigma = 0.001,
              z = 0.001),
    upper = c(b0 = Inf,
              b1 = Inf,
              a = Inf,
              mu = max(viro.sub$time),
              sigma = Inf,
              z = Inf),
    data = viro.sub)

summary(fit2)
```

### Model 3: Flat baseline + asymmetric Gaussian window

```{r}
# Starting values
B0 = min(viro.sub$y)
A = max(viro.sub$y) - min(viro.sub$y)
MU = viro.sub$time[which.max(viro.sub$y)]
SIGMAL = 4
SIGMAR = 4
Z = sd(viro.sub$y)

fit3 <- mle2(y ~
    dnorm(mean = b0 +
          a * ifelse(time <= mu,
              exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)),
              exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2))),
          sd = z),
    start = list(b0 = B0, a = A, mu = MU,
                 sigmaL = SIGMAL, sigmaR = SIGMAR, z = Z),
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(b0 = -Inf,
              a = 0,
              mu = min(viro.sub$time),
              sigmaL = 0.001,
              sigmaR = 0.001,
              z = 0.001),
    upper = c(b0 = Inf,
              a = Inf,
              mu = max(viro.sub$time),
              sigmaL = Inf,
              sigmaR = Inf,
              z = Inf),
    data = viro.sub)

summary(fit3)
```

## Compare models

```{r}
# Compare models using AIC
AIC(fit1, fit2, fit3)

# Calculate delta AIC
aic <- AIC(fit1, fit2, fit3)

aic$deltaAIC <- aic$AIC - min(aic$AIC)

# Calculate AIC weights
aic$weight <- exp(-0.5 * aic$deltaAIC) /
              sum(exp(-0.5 * aic$deltaAIC))

aic
```


## Inferring entrapment window parameters from the estimates in fit 3

The asymmetric Gaussian model (fit 3) provides estimates of the timing and breadth of
the entrapment window. The peak occurs at `mu`. The breadth of the window is
described by the half-width at half-maximum (HWHM) on the early and late sides,
and by their sum, the full width at half-maximum (FWHM).

```{r}
# Extract coefficients from the best model
p <- coef(fit3)

# Extract parameters
mu <- p["mu"]
sigmaL <- p["sigmaL"]
sigmaR <- p["sigmaR"]

# Conversion from sigma to half-width at half-maximum
hwhm <- sqrt(2 * log(2))

# Calculate window parameters
HWHM_L <- hwhm * sigmaL
HWHM_R <- hwhm * sigmaR
FWHM <- HWHM_L + HWHM_R

# Asymmetry index
asymmetry <- (sigmaR - sigmaL) / (sigmaR + sigmaL)

# Ratio of right to left width
width_ratio <- sigmaR / sigmaL

# Half-maximum times
half_left <- mu - HWHM_L
half_right <- mu + HWHM_R

# Create table of window parameters
window <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c(
    "Peak time (h)",
    "Left HWHM (h)",
    "Right HWHM (h)",
    "FWHM (h)",
    "Left half-maximum time (h)",
    "Right half-maximum time (h)",
    "Asymmetry index",
    "Right / left width"
  ),
  Estimate = c(
    mu,
    HWHM_L,
    HWHM_R,
    FWHM,
    half_left,
    half_right,
    asymmetry,
    width_ratio
  )
)

window
```

```{r}
# Predicted log10 virospore concentration
y.pred.log <- p["b0"] +
  p["a"] *
  ifelse(
    x.pred <= p["mu"],
    exp(-(x.pred - p["mu"])^2 /

    exp(-(x.pred - p["mu"])^2 /
          (2 * p["sigmaR"]^2))

# Convert predictions to original virospore scale

# Add fitted curve

      col = "red",

      lwd = 3)

graphics.off()
```

# Come back here and run null model on all data 
# Adding in a null model; there is no effect of time or MOI and every observation is explained by one global mean (using the moi = 0.1 data)
```{r}
# Starting values for null model
M <- mean(viro.sub$y, na.rm = TRUE)
Z <- sd(viro.sub$y, na.rm = TRUE)

fit_null <- mle2(
  y ~ dnorm(
    mean = m,
    sd = z
  ),
  start = list(
    m = M,
    z = Z
  ),
  method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(
    m = -Inf,
    z = 0.001
  ),
  upper = c(
    m = Inf,
    z = Inf
  ),
  data = viro.sub
)
summary(fit_null)
```

## Compare models again, this time adding in the null

```{r}
# Compare models using AIC
AIC(fit1, fit2, fit3, fit_null)

# Calculate delta AIC
aic <- AIC(fit1, fit2, fit3, fit_null)

aic$deltaAIC <- aic$AIC - min(aic$AIC)

# Calculate AIC weights
aic$weight <- exp(-0.5 * aic$deltaAIC) /
              sum(exp(-0.5 * aic$deltaAIC))

aic
```

```{r}
)
```

Before incorporating MOI, it's important to see how well all of the data fits to model fit 3 given that was only on a subset of data

```{r}
# Probably also want to add y column and time column to viro
viro <- viro %>% 
  mutate(
    y = log10(virospores.ml),
    time = Infection.time.h
  )

# Make sure MOI is a factor
viro$MOI <- factor(viro$MOI, levels = c("0.1", "1", "10"))

# Filter out any na
viro.fit <- viro %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(y),
    is.finite(time),
    !is.na(MOI)
  )

# Starting values
B0 = min(viro.fit$y)
A = max(viro.fit$y) - min(viro.fit$y)
MU = viro.fit$time[which.max(viro.fit$y)]
SIGMAL = 4
SIGMAR = 4
Z = sd(viro.fit$y)

fit3_allmoi <- mle2(y ~
    dnorm(mean = b0 +
          a * ifelse(time <= mu,
              exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)),
              exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2))),
          sd = z),
    start = list(b0 = B0, a = A, mu = MU,
                 sigmaL = SIGMAL, sigmaR = SIGMAR, z = Z),
    method = "L-BFGS-B",
    lower = c(b0 = -Inf,
              a = 0,
              mu = min(viro.fit$time),
              sigmaL = 0.001,
              sigmaR = 0.001,
              z = 0.001),
    upper = c(b0 = Inf,
              a = Inf,
              mu = max(viro.fit$time),
              sigmaL = Inf,
              sigmaR = Inf,
              z = Inf),
    data = viro.fit)

summary(fit3_allmoi)
```

How to incorporate 3 levels of MOI?
```{r}
# Use viro df since that contains all MOI 
# Start with the asymmetric gaussian since that provides best fit above


# Inserting fit 3 model and 

B0 = min(viro.fit$y)
A = max(viro.fit$y) - min(viro.fit$y)
MU = viro.fit$time[which.max(viro.fit$y)]
SIGMAL = 4
SIGMAR = 4
Z = sd(viro.fit$y)
# Here we are asking if MOI changes the magnitude of virospore production assuming they peak at the same time and have the same curve shape?
fit_moi_a <- mle2(
  y ~ dnorm(
    mean = b0 +
      (
        a0 +
        a1 * (MOI == "1") + # incorporating moi by allowing peak amplitude (a) to change depending on which MOI group an observation belongs to
        a10 * (MOI == "10")
      ) *
      ifelse(
        time <= mu,
        exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)),
        exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2))
      ),
    sd = z
  ),

  start = list(
    b0 = B0,
    a0 = A,
    a1 = 0,
    a10 = 0,
    mu = MU,
    sigmaL = SIGMAL,
    sigmaR = SIGMAR,
    z = Z
  ),

  data = viro.fit
)
summary(fit_moi_a)
```

```{r}
# Next we will ask if optimum varies with MOI 
fit_moi_mu <- mle2(
  y ~ dnorm(
    mean = b0 +
      a * ifelse(
        time <= (
          mu0 +
          mu1 * (MOI == "1") +
          mu10 * (MOI == "10")
        ),

        exp(
          -(time -
              (
                mu0 +
                mu1 * (MOI == "1") +
                mu10 * (MOI == "10")
              )
          )^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)
        ),

        exp(
          -(time -
              (
                mu0 +
                mu1 * (MOI == "1") +
                mu10 * (MOI == "10")
              )
          )^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2)
        )
      ),
    sd = z
  ),

  start = list(
    b0 = B0,
    a = A,
    mu0 = MU,
    mu1 = 0,
    mu10 = 0,
    sigmaL = SIGMAL,
    sigmaR = SIGMAR,
    z = Z
  ),

  data = viro.fit
)

summary(fit_moi_mu)
```

```{r}
# Finally we will ask if MOI changes the width or if the asymmetry varies with MOI 
# Next we will ask if optimum varies with MOI 
fit_moi_sigma <- mle2(
  y ~ dnorm(
    mean = b0 +
      a * ifelse(
        time <= mu,

        exp(
          -(time - mu)^2 /
            (
              2 * (
                sigmaL0 +
                sigmaL1 * (MOI == "1") +
                sigmaL10 * (MOI == "10")
              )^2
            )
        ),

        exp(
          -(time - mu)^2 /
            (
              2 * (
                sigmaR0 +
                sigmaR1 * (MOI == "1") +
                sigmaR10 * (MOI == "10")
              )^2
            )
        )
      ),
    sd = z
  ),

  start = list(
    b0 = B0,
    a = A,
    mu = MU,
    sigmaL0 = SIGMAL,
    sigmaL1 = 0,
    sigmaL10 = 0,
    sigmaR0 = SIGMAR,
    sigmaR1 = 0,
    sigmaR10 = 0,
    z = Z
  ),

  data = viro.fit
)
summary(fit_moi_sigma)
```

```{r}
# I was thinking we could compare model that fits MOI to previous model, but previous model included moi = 0.1, so that wouldn't be a fair comparison ; need to compare against model3 fit with all data

AIC(fit_moi_a, fit_moi_mu, fit_moi_sigma, fit3_allmoi)

# Calculate delta AIC
aic_moi <- AIC(fit_moi_a, fit_moi_mu, fit_moi_sigma, fit3_allmoi)

aic_moi$deltaAIC <- aic_moi$AIC - min(aic_moi$AIC)

# Calculate AIC weights
aic_moi$weight <- exp(-0.5 * aic_moi$deltaAIC) /
              sum(exp(-0.5 * aic_moi$deltaAIC))

aic_moi
```
```{r}
# Calculate complete MOI table
models <- list(
  "Common asymmetric" = fit3_allmoi,
  "MOI affects amplitude" = fit_moi_a,
  "MOI affects optimum" = fit_moi_mu,
  "MOI affects asymmetry" = fit_moi_sigma
)

aic_table <- data.frame(
  model = names(models),
  AIC = sapply(models, AIC),
  df = sapply(models, function(x) attr(logLik(x), "df"))
)

aic_table <- aic_table %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  mutate(
    deltaAIC = AIC - min(AIC),
    weight = exp(-0.5 * deltaAIC) /
      sum(exp(-0.5 * deltaAIC))
  )

aic_table
```

```{r}
mtext("Infection time (h)",
      side = 1,
      outer = TRUE,
      cex = 1.5,
      line = -4,
      adj = 0.5)

mtext(expression(paste("Virospores (mL"^{-1}, ")")),
      side = 2,
      outer = TRUE,
      cex = 1.5,
      line = -3.5,
      adj = 0.55)

# Extract fit3 coefficients
p <- coef(fit3_allmoi)

# Infection times for predicted curve
x.pred <- seq(0, 24, length.out = 1000)

# Predicted log10 virospore concentration
y.pred.log <- p["b0"] +
  p["a"] *
  ifelse(
    x.pred <= p["mu"],
    exp(-(x.pred - p["mu"])^2 /
          (2 * p["sigmaL"]^2)),
    exp(-(x.pred - p["mu"])^2 /
          (2 * p["sigmaR"]^2))
  )

# Convert predictions to original virospore scale
y.pred <- 10^y.pred.log

# Add fitted curve
lines(x.pred, y.pred,
      col = "red",
      lty = 1,
      lwd = 3)

# Close plot device
dev.off()
graphics.off()

# Show plot
img <- readPNG("~/GitHub/VirosporeQuant/Optimal.entrap/Figures/fit3_allmoi.png")
grid.raster(img)
```
# Now that we have a model that best fits our data let's try to figure out entrapment window
# Trying the half maximum method -- even though that doesn't answer our question fully, it's a way to start 
```{r}
# This is a repeat of what Jay calculated above essentially
pars <- coef(fit3_allmoi)
mu <- pars["mu"]
sigmaL <- pars["sigmaL"]
sigmaR <- pars["sigmaR"]

left_half <- mu - sigmaL * sqrt(2 * log(2))
right_half <- mu + sigmaR * sqrt(2 * log(2))

window <- right_half - left_half

c(
  optimum = mu,
  window_start = left_half,
  window_end = right_half,
  window_width = window
)
```

These results above suggest that:
1) the optimum time of infection is 14.88 h 
2) 50% window start is 2.91 h (fitted response reaches 50% maximum above baseline)
3) 50% window end 16.78 h (fitted response falls below 50% maximum above baseline)
4) Window width (FWHM) 13.87 (the duration of time which fitted production is >= 50% of maximum above baseline)

But this doesn't really answer the question about when entrapment can start and when the cutoff is (absolute)

Also the 50% cut off is arbitrary, so we need to be specific of the question we are asking

A different way to calculate the entrapment window
```{r}
coef(fit3_allmoi)
summary(fit3_allmoi)
fit3_allmoi@call
```
Trying another way to get optimum entrapment window, half maximum methods are intuitive but may not be meaningful for asymmetric curve, we can try another way by defining the window based on how much predictured entrapment is retained relative to the optimum, rather than defaulting to 50%
Wq is simply a threshold-defined near optimal window

There's also the issue that we have a non-zero baseline
```{r}
# Run this with best fit model
# Extract fitted parameters of best fit model
pars <- coef(fit3_allmoi)

b0     <- unname(pars["b0"])
a      <- unname(pars["a"])
mu     <- unname(pars["mu"])
sigmaL <- unname(pars["sigmaL"])
sigmaR <- unname(pars["sigmaR"])
# Choose threshold
q <- 0.75

# Create fine time grid
time_grid <- data.frame(
  time = seq(
    min(viro.fit$time),
    max(viro.fit$time),
    length.out = 10000
  )
)

# Calculate predicted response from fit3_allmoi
time_grid$predicted <- with(
  time_grid,
  b0 + a * ifelse(
    time <= mu,
    exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)),
    exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2))
  )
)

# Predicted maximum
max_pred <- b0 + a

# q threshold ABOVE BASELINE
threshold <- b0 + q * a

# Keep times where predicted response is >= threshold
window_data <- time_grid %>%
  dplyr::filter(predicted >= threshold)

# Calculate Wq
Wq <- data.frame(
  q = q,
  threshold = threshold,
  window_start = min(window_data$time),
  optimum = mu,
  window_end = max(window_data$time)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    window_width = window_end - window_start,
    pre_optimum_width = optimum - window_start,
    post_optimum_width = window_end - optimum
  )

Wq
```
Wq is the range of infection times over which the modeled entrapment response retains at least 75% of its maximum elevation above baseline
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

plot_wq <- ggplot(time_grid, aes(x = time, y = predicted)) +

  # Shade W75 region under fitted curve
  geom_ribbon(
    data = subset(
      time_grid,
      time >= Wq$window_start &
      time <= Wq$window_end
    ),
    aes(
      ymin = b0,
      ymax = predicted
    ),
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +

  # Fitted curve
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # 75% threshold
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = threshold,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  # Baseline
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = b0,
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  # Window boundaries
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(
      Wq$window_start,
      Wq$window_end
    ),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  # Optimum
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = Wq$optimum,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Infection time (h)",
    y = "Predicted entrapment response"
  ) 

plot_wq
```
A more direct way 

```{r}
pars <- coef(fit3_allmoi)

b0     <- unname(pars["b0"])
a      <- unname(pars["a"])
mu     <- unname(pars["mu"])
sigmaL <- unname(pars["sigmaL"])
sigmaR <- unname(pars["sigmaR"])

q <- 0.75

window_start <- mu - sigmaL * sqrt(-2 * log(q))
window_end   <- mu + sigmaR * sqrt(-2 * log(q))

threshold <- b0 + q * a

Wq <- data.frame(
  q = q,
  threshold = threshold,
  window_start = window_start,
  optimum = mu,
  window_end = window_end,
  window_width = window_end - window_start,
  pre_optimum_width = mu - window_start,
  post_optimum_width = window_end - mu
)

Wq
```
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Extract parameters
pars <- coef(fit3_allmoi)

b0     <- unname(pars["b0"])
a      <- unname(pars["a"])
mu     <- unname(pars["mu"])
sigmaL <- unname(pars["sigmaL"])
sigmaR <- unname(pars["sigmaR"])

# Define q
q <- 0.75

# Calculate exact window
window_start <- mu - sigmaL * sqrt(-2 * log(q))
window_end   <- mu + sigmaR * sqrt(-2 * log(q))
threshold    <- b0 + q * a

# Generate fitted curve
curve_df <- data.frame(
  time = seq(
    min(viro.fit$time),
    max(viro.fit$time),
    length.out = 1000
  )
)

curve_df$predicted <- with(
  curve_df,
  b0 + a * ifelse(
    time <= mu,
    exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaL^2)),
    exp(-(time - mu)^2 / (2 * sigmaR^2))
  )
)
```

```{r}
plot_window <- ggplot() +

  # Shade the 75% window
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = window_start,
    xmax = window_end,
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf,
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # Raw data
  geom_point(
    data = viro.fit,
    aes(x = time, y = y),
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  # Fitted asymmetric Gaussian
  geom_line(
    data = curve_df,
    aes(x = time, y = predicted),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +

  # 75% threshold
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = threshold,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Window boundaries
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(window_start, window_end),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Optimum
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mu,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

labs(
  x = "Infection time (h)",
  y = expression(log[10]*"(virospores/mL)")
)

plot_window
```
